intended_object: The connecting homomorphism H_i(X₃) → H_j(X₁) attached to a short exact sequence 0 → X₁ → X₂ → X₃ → 0 of homological complexes in an abelian category, where c.Rel i j holds (the differential goes from degree i to degree j). Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The definition is faithful: it is the standard connecting homomorphism, built the textbook way with the snake lemma.

It takes the connecting map δ of a snake-lemma diagram (`snakeInput`). That diagram is built from the short exact sequence of complexes, using the functors for homology, opcycles and cycles. Its middle rows are opcycles in degree i and cycles in degree j. The vertical map between them is the one the differential induces. The rows of homology in degrees i and j appear as the kernels and cokernels of that map. Applying the snake lemma gives H_i(X₃) → H_j(X₁).

The library goes on to prove the expected properties: `δ_comp`, `comp_δ`, and exactness of the long homology sequence at each place (`homology_exact₁` and the following lemmas).

The setting is fully general: any abelian category, any complex shape, and any pair of degrees with c.Rel i j. This is Mathlib's own general definition, so there is no broader version to point to.
